title: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still
body:
Read the chapter → [Joshua 10](/bible/joshua/10)

**[Joshua 10:1-5](/bible/joshua/10#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/10#v1)</sup> Now it came to pass, when Adoni–zedek king of Jerusalem had heard how Joshua had taken Ai, and had utterly destroyed it; as he had done to Jericho and her king, so he had done to Ai and her king; and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and were among them;
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/joshua/10#v2)</sup> That they feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/joshua/10#v3)</sup> Wherefore Adoni–zedek king of Jerusalem sent unto Hoham king of Hebron, and unto Piram king of Jarmuth, and unto Japhia king of Lachish, and unto Debir king of Eglon, saying,
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/joshua/10#v4)</sup> Come up unto me, and help me, that we may smite Gibeon: for it hath made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/joshua/10#v5)</sup> Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together, and went up, they and all their hosts, and encamped before Gibeon, and made war against it.

- Adoni-zedec king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai and utterly destroyed it. You might be confused why it says Jerusalem, since Jerusalem had not been set up as of yet because the land was not conquered: when the scribes wrote the history they left identifying location markers, so the reader knows visually where this is taking place.
- They feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty. So the five kings of the Amorites, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon, gathered themselves, went up with all their hosts, and made war against Gibeon, because it had made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 14:14](/bible/genesis/14#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/genesis/14#v14)</sup> And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.

    Abram pursued them unto Dan, yet the land of Dan was not established in Genesis and Israel was not even born yet; proof the scribes leave location markers for the reader.

**[Joshua 10:6-9](/bible/joshua/10#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/10#v6)</sup> And the men of Gibeon sent unto Joshua to the camp to Gilgal, saying, Slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us: for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/10#v7)</sup> So Joshua ascended from Gilgal, he, and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valour.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/10#v8)</sup> And the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/joshua/10#v9)</sup> Joshua therefore came unto them suddenly, and went up from Gilgal all night.

- The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at Gilgal: slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us.
- The LORD said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. So Joshua ascended from Gilgal all night with all the people of war and the mighty men of valour, and came unto them suddenly.

**[Joshua 10:10-11](/bible/joshua/10#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/joshua/10#v10)</sup> And the Lord discomfited them before Israel, and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Beth–horon, and smote them to Azekah, and unto Makkedah.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/joshua/10#v11)</sup> And it came to pass, as they fled from before Israel, and were in the going down to Beth–horon, that the Lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died: they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword.

- The LORD discomfited them before Israel, slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Beth-horon. As they fled, the LORD cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died.
- They were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. The Most High was up in heaven aiming the hailstones right at the people, and nobody could escape.
- He did the same thing in Egypt: the elements were changed in themselves to fight for Israel, and here he sends down hailstones to destroy the people again.

  Precepts:
  - **[Wisdom of Solomon 19:18-20](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/19#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/19#v18)</sup> For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, like as in a psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds; which may well be perceived by the sight of the things that have been done.
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/19#v19)</sup> For earthly things were turned into watery, and the things, that before swam in the water, now went upon the ground.
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/19#v20)</sup> The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own virtue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature.

    As in Egypt, the elements themselves were changed to fight against Israel's enemies.

**[Joshua 10:12-14](/bible/joshua/10#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/joshua/10#v12)</sup> Then spake Joshua to the Lord in the day when the Lord delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/joshua/10#v13)</sup> And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/joshua/10#v14)</sup> And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the Lord hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the Lord fought for Israel.

- Joshua spake to the LORD in the sight of Israel: Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. The sun stood still in the midst of heaven and hasted not to go down about a whole day, and there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel.
- Is not this written in the book of Jasher? Why do we not have that book today? The mouth of the Most High commanded and his spirit gathered the books of the Bible for us in these last days; he left the book of Jasher out because we do not need it in this captivity. If he wanted us to read it, he would have left it in the book.
- He put the Apocrypha in the 1611 version because he wanted us to read it in the last days; the Protestants and Catholics took it out of the modern Bible in the late 1700s, but you cannot stop the Most High. The Bible will always be with the children of Israel, and no, a white man did not write it: the Most High put it in the hands of our enemies to preserve it. That is the power of God.
- Reading is fundamental. Listening to and watching videos is fine, but nothing takes the place of reading; the hearing of the word strengthens the understanding of what we have read. That is why the leadership set up the four chapters reading, so make sure reading is first and foremost in understanding and applying the words of the Most High.
- Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 34:16-17](/bible/isaiah/34#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/isaiah/34#v16)</sup> Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/isaiah/34#v17)</sup> And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.

    Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no prophecy in it shall fail, and the land is divided to Israel from generation to generation, so the book follows the children of Israel forever.
  - **[Ecclesiastes 12:12](/bible/ecclesiastes/12#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/ecclesiastes/12#v12)</sup> And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

    Of making many books there is no end, and much study of books he did not command is a weariness of the flesh.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 3:21-24](/bible/sirach/3#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/sirach/3#v21)</sup> Seek not out things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/sirach/3#v22)</sup> But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret.
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/sirach/3#v23)</sup> Be not curious in unnecessary matters: for more things are shewed unto thee than men understand.
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/sirach/3#v24)</sup> For many are deceived by their own vain opinion; and an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment.

    Be not curious in unnecessary matters; think with reverence on what is commanded thee.

**[Joshua 10:15-21](/bible/joshua/10#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/joshua/10#v15)</sup> And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, unto the camp to Gilgal.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/joshua/10#v16)</sup> But these five kings fled, and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/joshua/10#v17)</sup> And it was told Joshua, saying, The five kings are found hid in a cave at Makkedah.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/joshua/10#v18)</sup> And Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, and set men by it for to keep them:
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/joshua/10#v19)</sup> And stay ye not, but pursue after your enemies, and smite the hindmost of them; suffer them not to enter into their cities: for the Lord your God hath delivered them into your hand.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/joshua/10#v20)</sup> And it came to pass, when Joshua and the children of Israel had made an end of slaying them with a very great slaughter, till they were consumed, that the rest which remained of them entered into fenced cities.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/joshua/10#v21)</sup> And all the people returned to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace: none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.

- The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, set men by it to keep them, and stay ye not: pursue after your enemies and smite the hindmost of them, for the LORD your God hath delivered them into your hand.
- Israel slew them with a very great slaughter till they were consumed, and none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Those dogs equal nations.
- Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 11:7](/bible/exodus/11#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/11#v7)</sup> But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.

    Against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, that ye may know how that the LORD doth put a difference between Egypt and Israel; underline it and put Joshua 10:20-21 next to it.
  - **[Matthew 15:24-26](/bible/matthew/15#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/matthew/15#v24)</sup> But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/matthew/15#v25)</sup> Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/matthew/15#v26)</sup> But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.

    I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel; it is not meet to take the children's bread and to cast it to dogs; Christ called the other nations dogs just as Exodus 11:7 and Joshua 10:21 do.

**[Joshua 10:22-25](/bible/joshua/10#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/joshua/10#v22)</sup> Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me out of the cave.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/joshua/10#v23)</sup> And they did so, and brought forth those five kings unto him out of the cave, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/joshua/10#v24)</sup> And it came to pass, when they brought out those kings unto Joshua, that Joshua called for all the men of Israel, and said unto the captains of the men of war which went with him, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. And they came near, and put their feet upon the necks of them.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/joshua/10#v25)</sup> And Joshua said unto them, Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.

- Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
- Joshua called for all the men of Israel and said to the captains of the men of war, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the LORD do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.
- They hid in caves, and that is what the nations are going to do again. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy: in the day of the Most High men shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 2:10-12](/bible/isaiah/2#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/isaiah/2#v10)</sup> Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/isaiah/2#v11)</sup> The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/isaiah/2#v12)</sup> For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low:

    Enter into the rock and hide thee in the dust for fear of the LORD; caves are made out of rock, and the day of the LORD is upon everyone that is proud and lofty.
  - **[Isaiah 2:19-21](/bible/isaiah/2#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/isaiah/2#v19)</sup> And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/isaiah/2#v20)</sup> In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats;
    >
    > <sup>[21](/bible/isaiah/2#v21)</sup> To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

    They shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth; a future prophecy.

**[Joshua 10:26-27](/bible/joshua/10#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/joshua/10#v26)</sup> And afterward Joshua smote them, and slew them, and hanged them on five trees: and they were hanging upon the trees until the evening.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/joshua/10#v27)</sup> And it came to pass at the time of the going down of the sun, that Joshua commanded, and they took them down off the trees, and cast them into the cave wherein they had been hid, and laid great stones in the cave’s mouth, which remain until this very day.

- Afterward Joshua smote them, slew them, and hanged them on five trees until the evening; at the going down of the sun they took them down, cast them into the cave wherein they had been hid, and laid great stones in the cave's mouth, which remain until this very day.
- They took them down according to the law: he that is hanged is accursed of God, and the body shall not remain all night upon the tree, that thy land be not defiled.
- Everybody that is hung from a tree is cursed. That lets you know all the nations are cursed, and Israel fell up under the curses also.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 21:22-23](/bible/deuteronomy/21#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/21#v22)</sup> And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/deuteronomy/21#v23)</sup> His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.

    His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, for he that is hanged is accursed of God; they took the kings down so the land would not be defiled.

**[Joshua 10:28-39](/bible/joshua/10#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/joshua/10#v28)</sup> And that day Joshua took Makkedah, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and the king thereof he utterly destroyed, them, and all the souls that were therein; he let none remain: and he did to the king of Makkedah as he did unto the king of Jericho.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/joshua/10#v29)</sup> Then Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, unto Libnah, and fought against Libnah:
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/joshua/10#v30)</sup> And the Lord delivered it also, and the king thereof, into the hand of Israel; and he smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls that were therein; he let none remain in it; but did unto the king thereof as he did unto the king of Jericho.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/joshua/10#v31)</sup> And Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, unto Lachish, and encamped against it, and fought against it:
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/joshua/10#v32)</sup> And the Lord delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel, which took it on the second day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls that were therein, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/joshua/10#v33)</sup> Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua smote him and his people, until he had left him none remaining.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/joshua/10#v34)</sup> And from Lachish Joshua passed unto Eglon, and all Israel with him; and they encamped against it, and fought against it:
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/joshua/10#v35)</sup> And they took it on that day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls that were therein he utterly destroyed that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/joshua/10#v36)</sup> And Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, unto Hebron; and they fought against it:
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/joshua/10#v37)</sup> And they took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and the king thereof, and all the cities thereof, and all the souls that were therein; he left none remaining, according to all that he had done to Eglon; but destroyed it utterly, and all the souls that were therein.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/joshua/10#v38)</sup> And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to Debir; and fought against it:
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/joshua/10#v39)</sup> And he took it, and the king thereof, and all the cities thereof; and they smote them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed all the souls that were therein; he left none remaining: as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir, and to the king thereof; as he had done also to Libnah, and to her king.

- That day Joshua took Makkedah and smote it with the edge of the sword; he utterly destroyed all the souls that were therein, he let none remain, and did to the king of Makkedah as he did unto the king of Jericho.
- The southern campaign rolled city by city: Libnah, then Lachish, which he took on the second day; Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua smote him and his people until he had left him none remaining.
- From Lachish to Eglon, up to Hebron, and back to Debir: every city taken, its king slain, and all the souls therein utterly destroyed, none remaining, according to all that he had done to the cities before.

**[Joshua 10:40-43](/bible/joshua/10#v40)**

> <sup>[40](/bible/joshua/10#v40)</sup> So Joshua smote all the country of the hills, and of the south, and of the vale, and of the springs, and all their kings: he left none remaining, but utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the Lord God of Israel commanded.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/joshua/10#v41)</sup> And Joshua smote them from Kadesh–barnea even unto Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even unto Gibeon.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/joshua/10#v42)</sup> And all these kings and their land did Joshua take at one time, because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/joshua/10#v43)</sup> And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, unto the camp to Gilgal.

- So Joshua smote all the country of the hills, of the south, of the vale, and of the springs, and all their kings; he left none remaining, but utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the LORD God of Israel commanded, from Kadesh-barnea even unto Gaza. All these kings did Joshua take at one time, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
- This is why they tell you not to read the Old Testament: the Most High is out there fighting through his people, giving them the spirit to destroy all that breathe, both young and old, leaving none alive. The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.
- Do not think the Most High is unjust in what he does. Nobody taught him or took counsel with him; you cannot show him anything, because he made you and you just got here. In his infinite wisdom he decreed in his own counsel that the nations are as a drop of a bucket, counted as the small dust of the balance that does not tip the scale at all.
- Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering: you could not gather enough wood or sacrifice enough animals to change his mind about the other nations. All nations before him are as nothing, and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. All means all: no nation is excluded. No wonder the Most High gave Moses and Joshua the green light to destroy everything that breathed.
- He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 15:3](/bible/exodus/15#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/15#v3)</sup> The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

    The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.
  - **[Isaiah 40:13-17](/bible/isaiah/40#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/isaiah/40#v13)</sup> Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him?
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/isaiah/40#v14)</sup> With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/isaiah/40#v15)</sup> Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/isaiah/40#v16)</sup> And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/isaiah/40#v17)</sup> All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.

    Who hath directed the spirit of the LORD, or taught him? The nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.
  - **[Job 12:23](/bible/job/12#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/job/12#v23)</sup> He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.

    He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them.
